title: How selected healthcare accountability routes are structured
caution: This describes selected public mechanisms and their published structures. It does not rank provinces, compare harms or measure effectiveness.

mechanisms.mechanism: Patient Care Quality Offices and Review Boards

fields.label: Complaint entry point
fields.value: A health authority Patient Care Quality Office is the first step for complaints about health-authority care.

fields.label: Investigator or reviewer
fields.value: The health authority office processes the complaint; an independent Review Board can review unresolved concerns after that response.

fields.label: Institutional home
fields.value: Complaint offices sit within health authorities. Review Boards are statutory provincial boards.

fields.label: Indigenous-specific mechanism
fields.value: The statutory route is general. Health authorities have added Indigenous complaint liaisons and related processes, and the 2026 provincial review explicitly includes Indigenous-specific racism.

fields.label: Published authority
fields.value: Review Boards can review complaints, report findings and actions, and make recommendations to health authorities or the minister.

fields.label: Recommendations
fields.value: Recommendations may address patient-care quality or complaint processes; they are advisory rather than disciplinary orders.

fields.label: Appeal or reconsideration
fields.value: A Review Board is the published second-stage review after the health authority office. A further appeal route is not clearly stated on the public process pages reviewed.

fields.label: Public reporting
fields.value: The Act requires Review Boards to report annually to the minister; public reports have been posted by the Boards.

fields.label: Aggregate outcome reporting
fields.value: The Act provides for reporting complaint and review volumes and resolution times. Current Indigenous-specific public disaggregation varies and was not located as one provincewide ledger.

fields.label: Implementation follow-up
fields.value: In Plain Sight follow-up records health-authority complaint-process changes, while the province's wider quality-review reform remains underway.

fields.label: Indigenous governance or input
fields.value: The current reform includes sessions with First Nations and Métis communities. Published materials describe engagement; they do not by themselves establish shared governance of the statutory Boards.

fields.label: Major transparency gap
fields.value: No single current public view was located that connects Indigenous-specific complaints, recommendations and implementation across all health authorities.

mechanisms.mechanism: Indigenous Patient Safety Investigator and Advocate

fields.label: Complaint entry point
fields.value: First Nations, Métis and Inuit patients or families can contact the Office of Alberta Health Advocates by phone, email or web inquiry.

fields.label: Investigator or reviewer
fields.value: The Indigenous Patient Safety Investigator and Advocate supports navigation and may conduct a delegated Health Charter review where no other dispute process exists.

fields.label: Institutional home
fields.value: The role is part of the provincial Office of Alberta Health Advocates under the Ministry of Primary and Preventative Health Services.

fields.label: Indigenous-specific mechanism
fields.value: The role is specifically available to First Nations, Métis and Inuit patients and families with concerns about Alberta health-care services.

fields.label: Published authority
fields.value: Published functions include support, early resolution, referral, delegated Health Charter review, system advice and recommendations. The role cannot reverse decisions, discipline providers or impose penalties.

fields.label: Recommendations
fields.value: The mandate permits recommendations to government and professional organizations, but no role-specific public recommendation ledger was located.

fields.label: Appeal or reconsideration
fields.value: A role-specific appeal or reconsideration process was not clearly stated on the public pages reviewed.

fields.label: Public reporting
fields.value: A ministry business plan now includes a role-specific correspondence measure. No comprehensive role-specific annual outcome report was located.

fields.label: Aggregate outcome reporting
fields.value: The business plan reports 321 correspondence items in 2025. It does not disaggregate accepted matters, completed reviews, recommendations, referrals, resolutions or outcomes.

fields.label: Implementation follow-up
fields.value: Appointment, operation and public education are documented; role-specific follow-up on recommendations and resulting changes was not located.

fields.label: Indigenous governance or input
fields.value: The mandate includes relationships with First Nations, Métis and Inuit representatives and access to Elders and Knowledge Keepers. Published governance or oversight terms were not located.

fields.label: Major transparency gap
fields.value: Correspondence volume is visible, but what happened after contact remains mostly unavailable in role-specific aggregate reporting.

fields.label: Complaint entry point
fields.value: First Nations people in Saskatchewan can contact FNHO directly for advocacy, navigation, complaint resolution or investigation support.

fields.label: Investigator or reviewer
fields.value: FNHO describes advocacy, mediation, investigation and systemic-recommendation functions.

fields.label: Institutional home
fields.value: FNHO is a First Nations-governed office, separate from the Saskatchewan Health Authority and provincial government.

fields.label: Indigenous-specific mechanism
fields.value: The office serves First Nations people in Saskatchewan and describes its authority through the FSIN Chiefs-in-Assembly.

fields.label: Published authority
fields.value: FNHO describes independent advocacy, mediation and investigation, with recommendations and referrals. Its public pages do not describe coercive enforcement powers.

fields.label: Recommendations
fields.value: The inaugural report presents recommendations and systemic themes directed toward healthcare organizations and public institutions.

fields.label: Appeal or reconsideration
fields.value: A formal appeal or reconsideration route for FNHO decisions was not clearly stated on the public pages reviewed.

fields.label: Public reporting
fields.value: FNHO published an inaugural 2023–2025 report with aggregate complaint and activity information.

fields.label: Aggregate outcome reporting
fields.value: The inaugural report records 391 complaints, with 224 closed or resolved and 167 active; 64% related to the Saskatchewan Health Authority.

fields.label: Implementation follow-up
fields.value: A ministerial statement said the Ministry and Saskatchewan Health Authority were reviewing the report. A later comprehensive public response or implementation ledger was not located in the bounded review.

fields.label: Indigenous governance or input
fields.value: FNHO describes governance authority through the FSIN Chiefs-in-Assembly. Public funding support is distinct from that governance relationship.

fields.label: Major transparency gap
fields.value: The office reports its own activity, but a recommendation-by-recommendation public response from Saskatchewan institutions was not located.
